newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end lower in lower volume.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end lower in lower volume.

text.p: French shares finished in loss on Tuesday, after running into profit-taking. Traders said volumes were relatively thin, following the start of the holiday season.
Sentiment was also dented by sharp falls in London equities, sparked by fears of higher U.K. interest rates, they added.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 17.85 points or 0.61 percent at 2,929.81. The CAC-40 futures contract was down 19 at 2,936 from Monday's close.
Volume was a thin 7.19 billion francs compared to the double-digit figures seen in recent weeks.

* Alcatel Alsthom ends down 2.02 percent at 775. Chairman Serge Tchuruk told Reuters he wanted more details of GEC's plans for demerging the GEC Alsthom rail and power joint venture that include a possible flotation.
One leading French broker estimated GEC Alsthom's market capitalisation at 45 billion francs.
A GEC Alsthom flotation could help fund Alcatel's bid for Thomson-CSF TCFP.PA. The defence electronics firm closed up 3.16 percent at 172.9.
* Eurotunnel EUTL.PA gains 3.66 percent to 8.50 francs, as the market bets on approval of debt plan on Thursday.
Eurotunnel shareholders vote on the debt restructuring on Thursday.
* Cap Gemini said after the close it expected an 80 percent rise in net attributable profit for 1997.
* The car sector got a lift, reversing recent weakness, with Renault up 2.2 percent at 143.70 francs, and PSA Peugeot Citroen adding 1.58 percent at 579.
Michelin gained 2.95 percent at 376.90, while Bertrand Faure added 0.25 percent to 322.60.

French senator Yvon Collin of the finance committee urged the merger of Dassault and Aerospatiale, to build a powerful national aircraft company and a recapitalisation of Aerospatiale to make it competitive against U.S. giants.
